subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool silently corrupts 2>&1 / 2>/dev/null shell redirect arguments

question: Is the shipped v2026.5.27 redirect-corruption report enough to schedule a current-main live repro/debug pass, or should maintainers close it as not reproducible from current source inspection?
rationale: Current source inspection shows the normal exec paths preserving one command string, but the user report is concrete and no live current-main path has proved or disproved the mutation boundary.

options.title: Run current-main live repro
options.body: Exercise a real OpenClaw/Codex exec call with `gh ... 2>&1` and `2>/dev/null`, then fix only the boundary that mutates the command text if it still reproduces.

options.title: Close as no-repro
options.body: Close the issue if maintainers consider the current source and existing redirect-preservation test coverage sufficient to rule out a main-branch bug.

recommendation.title: Run current-main live repro
recommendation.body: Exercise a real OpenClaw/Codex exec call with `gh ... 2>&1` and `2>/dev/null`, then fix only the boundary that mutates the command text if it still reproduces.

likelyOwner.reason: The most likely next decision is around exec authorization/current-main repro boundaries, where this history is strongest.
